title: C5: finiteness on proper curves
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a
smooth proper connected curve over $k$, let
$r$ be a prime (arbitrary, possibly
$r=\operatorname{char}k$), and let
$\mathbf F_r$ be the constant sheaf, viewed as constructible. Then
$\mathbf F_r$ satisfies $\mathcal C_5(C,\mathbf F_r)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]: $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)$
is finite for every $q\geq0$.

proof.text: If r is nonzero in k apply C4. Otherwise CharP.charP_iff_prime_eq_zero supplies CharP k r. Degree zero is finite by connected constant-sheaf H0 and the proved finite coefficient biproduct argument. Degrees above one vanish by C3.

In degree one, the zero-dimensional case follows from zero_dimensional_etale_cohomology_rest and the Ext/derived comparison. In dimension one use the Artin-Schreier sequence and apply derived global sections to its distinguished triangle. The degree-zero Artin-Schreier map is epi; the homology sequence then makes the degree-one inclusion mono.

Use the proper specialization of the finite scalar model for additive H1. With φ = wp + id, naturality of sectionwise scalar multiplication shows that H1(φ) is p-semilinear. Its difference from the identity is H1(wp). Hence the kernel of H1(wp) injects into the finite Frobenius-fixed subgroup. The composite of the degree-one inclusion with H1(wp) is zero, so the mono above injects H1(C,ZMod r) into this finite kernel.
Transport the finite derived degree-one group to Ext cohomology, then transfer finiteness to Λ/(r) through the finite coefficient biproduct coordinates proved in this module.
